key_insight: A physics-grounded digital twin can rapidly de-risk robotic in-space welding by combining thermal simulation, surrogate models, and control to screen process settings before costly experiments.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports safer design of orbital metal-joining systems by predicting weld quality and controller behavior under reduced-gravity, low-pressure conditions.
method: Finite-volume weld-pool model with solid-liquid phase change, effective thermocapillary transport, and local-pressure effects
Gaussian-process and neural-network surrogates trained and validated with repeated five-fold cross-validation
Simulated six-axis manipulator and UR5 L-shaped-seam control study using a proportional controller
evidence_signal: The GP outperformed the neural network on all eight outputs in repeated five-fold cross-validation, 74/80 held-out solver responses fell within 90% predictive intervals, and a three-output GP query took 249 microseconds.
watch_item: The results are simulation-based, so thermal-vacuum, reduced-gravity, and hardware-in-the-loop testing are still needed to confirm real-world robustness.
paper_title: De-Risking Robotic Welding for In-Space Metal Joining Through Physics-Grounded Digital Twins
